newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy expects improvement in second half.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy expects improvement in second half.

text.p: Best Buy Co Inc, which earlier Wednesday reported a loss for the first quarter, said it expects operating performance to improve in the second half of the year.

"We expect that as we move into the seasonally higher volume second half of the fiscal year and continue to build upon our initiatives to improve profits, our operating performance will strongly improve over fiscal 1997," said Best Buy Chairman and Chief Executive Richard Schulze in a statement.

Best Buy plans to open 13 stores this year. Two were opened in the first quarter, six more are scheduled to open this quarter and the rest will be launched in the third quarter, the consumer electronics retailer said.

Best Buy recently reduced the seasonal capacity of its unsecured revolving credit facility to $365 million due to slower store growth and improved inventory management, Best Buy said. The bank group providing the facility, led by First Bank National Association, as agent, lowered Best Buy's interest coverage ratio requirement through maturity in June of 1998.

During the first quarter, gross profit margin was 15.4 percent, an increase of 1.2 percent of sales from the 14.2 percent level reported in the first quarter of last year, Best Buy said. The improvement is due to higher product margins, a continuation of the increasing contribution from performance service plans and reduction in the use of extended consumer financing offers.
Performance service plan sales were 2.9 percent of store sales compared to 1.5 percent of sales in the first quarter of last year.

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased to 15.1 percent of sales versus 13.4 percent in last year's first quarter as the decline in comparable store sales hurt leverage on operating expenses.
